### Description

In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn how to transform standard ggplot2 outputs into clear, polished, publication-ready figures. Working through practical examples, we will cover:

- building **custom themes** for a consistent look
- choosing **colour** scales with intent (intuitive and colourblind-safe palettes)
- composing **multi-panel layouts** with `patchwork`
- **exporting** figures at the resolution and dimensions journals expect

Along the way I will show you a few useful extension packages from the ggplot2 ecosystem (`ggtext`, `ggrepel`, `gghighlight`, `ggdist`, `ggridges`) so you can pick up techniques you can apply directly to your own plots.

### Workshop materials

The workshop repo contains all demo scripts, exercises, and solutions:

## Resources

### 1. Custom themes

- [`theme()` reference](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html) doc for every theme argument
- [`ggthemes`](https://jrnold.github.io/ggthemes/): ready-made themes if you don't want to build your own

### 2. Colour

- [Which color scale to use](https://blog.datawrapper.de/which-color-scale-to-use-in-data-vis/): Blogpost by Lisa Charlotte Muth, Datawrapper
- [Colour pitfalls (Wilke, *Fundamentals of Data Visualization*)](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/color-pitfalls.html): background on choosing colour and the Okabe-Ito and other CVD-safe palettes
- [`viridis`](https://sjmgarnier.github.io/viridis/): More info on the viridis palette colors
- [`scico`](https://github.com/thomasp85/scico) and [Fabio Crameri's colour maps](https://www.fabiocrameri.ch/colourmaps/) for scientific palettes, designed to be fair and citable
- [`colorBlindness`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=colorBlindness) to check your plots for colourblind accessibility

### 3. Multi-panel layouts with patchwork

- [patchwork documentation](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com/) is excellent and has a gallery of examples to browse

### 4. Exporting figures

- [Export module from ggplot2-uncharted workshop](https://www.ggplot2-uncharted.com/module1/export)
- [`ggview`](https://github.com/idmn/ggview) to preview a plot at its true size before exporting
- [`ragg`](https://ragg.r-lib.org/) for fast, high-quality raster device for PNG/TIFF

## Other handy packages

The official [ggplot extension gallery](https://exts.ggplot2.tidyverse.org/gallery/) lists ~120 community extension packages to browse


- [`gghighlight`](https://yutannihilation.github.io/gghighlight/) — fade non-focal data with one line
- [`ggrepel`](https://ggrepel.slowkow.com/) — non-overlapping text labels
- [`ggtext`](https://wilkelab.org/ggtext/) — markdown / HTML in titles, axis text, and annotations
- [`ggdist`](https://mjskay.github.io/ggdist/) — distributions and uncertainty (raincloud, halfeye, interval plots)
- [`ggridges`](https://wilkelab.org/ggridges/) — ridgeline / joy plots
